title: Compliance request lifecycle inspector and downloadable attestation bundles
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Overview: Customers regularly submit compliance requests asking for proof of where their customer data is stored, how long logs and KVs are retained, and a packaged bundle of evidence (DPAs, configuration snapshots, audit logs, and export manifests). This ticket proposes a lightweight orchestration layer — the Compliance Request Lifecycle Inspector (CRLI) — that guides an internal flow from request intake to a downloadable attestation bundle. CRLI will combine residency verification, retention configuration snapshotting, automated evidence collection, and an attestations generator supporting signed exports for enterprise auditors.

Problem to solve:
- Customers and internal CS teams spend hours manually collecting residency and retention artifacts for audits and DPA reviews.
- Current exports are ad-hoc CSVs and partial screenshots; there is no standard attestation or deterministic timeline.
- Engineers spend time re-running queries and verifying configs across Dedicated and Private deployments.

Goals:
1) Provide a single intake UI and API to accept compliance requests (region/residency checks, retention windows, DPA clauses).
2) Automate evidence collection (configuration snapshot, route-level logging samples, storage residency proofs, encryption/KMS metadata).
3) Produce a downloadable, signed attestation bundle (PDF + JSON manifest + hashes) with a human-readable timeline and machine-readable evidence map.
4) Expose a verification API for customers to programmatically fetch/validate attestation bundles.
5) Minimize manual operator effort; default success path should be fully automated for common requests.

Scope (in-scope):
- Intake form + API for standard compliance requests (residency + retention + DPA clause checkbox).
- Residency verifier that queries our deployment metadata and storage region mappings to assert where persisted KV and artifacts reside.
- Retention snapshot that records configured retention rules for logs, telemetry, and per-customer KV caches at time of request.
- Evidence collector that compiles config artifacts, recent audit log excerpts (timeboxed), and links to related PR/Change records.
- Attestation generator that creates a signed bundle (PDF + manifest.json + checksums) and stores it with an immutable identifier.

Out of scope:
- Implementing full legal sign-off for DPAs (legal will review attestation content but signing via Legal's e-signature provider is separate).
- Cross-region live data migration or deletion workflows (we surface retention settings and deletion proofs but do not perform deletions).

High-level design:
- Intake: new Console route + REST API endpoint /compliance/requests. Basic questionnaire fields and optional file upload for customer-supplied forms.
- Orchestrator: a serverless workflow that validates inputs, triggers evidence collectors (residency, retention, logs, KMS metadata), and aggregates artifacts into a staging area.
- Residency verifier: reads centralized infra metadata service and Dedicated/Private deployment registries; produces a region assertion with confidence level and supporting artifact links.
- Retention snapshot: reads config state (Console configs, infra retention policies, per-customer overrides), normalizes to a retention matrix and time-anchored snapshot.
- Evidence bundle: PDF summary (human readable), manifest.json (flat list of artifacts with SHA256 checksums and timestamps), optional redaction notes, and an attestation signature (platform signing key).
- Verification API: GET /compliance/attestations/{id} returns manifest and verification status.

Acceptance criteria (must):
- AC1: Console and API intake accept a residency+retention request and return a request id within 10s.
- AC2: Automated collector gathers residency proof and retention snapshot for hosted and Dedicated customers for 90% of requests without operator intervention.
- AC3: Generated attestation bundle contains a PDF summary, manifest.json, at least one supporting artifact per claim, and a platform signature; bundle is downloadable from Console and via API.
- AC4: Verification API returns consistent checksums and signature verification for any produced bundle.
- AC5: CS/Account teams can add private notes and mark a request as "requires manual review"; manual review path creates a changelog entry.

Telemetry & success metrics:
- Time-to-bundle (median target < 30 minutes for automated path).
- Automation rate (target >= 90% of requests succeed without manual steps).
- CS time saved (baseline surveys to measure).
- Number of audit escalations reduced.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Private on-prem deployments have incomplete metadata. Mitigation: fall back to an operator-assisted flow that flags required artifacts and provides a checklist for the customer.
- Risk: Legal disagreement on wording of attestation. Mitigation: include legal in drafting and provide versioned templates editable in Console.
- Risk: Signing key management. Mitigation: use HSM-backed platform signing and rotate keys per policy; record signing key id in manifest.

Rollout plan:
1) Alpha: internal CS + two pilot customers (hosted + Dedicated) to validate automation (4 weeks).
2) Beta: broader CRO and enterprise accounts, add verification API and error reporting (6 weeks).
3) GA: expose to all Console users, add audit trails and retention policy change detection (another 4 weeks).

Open questions:
- Q1: What legal language must be present in the PDF attestation for DPA adjuncts? (Owner: Legal)
- Q2: Should attestation bundles support time-limited signed URLs for external auditor access? (Owner: Product Security)
- Q3: How to surface per-route residency when routing policy performs live fallbacks to other regions? (Owner: Runtime team)
